long_biography.plain_text:
Born in Agadir, Rivière moved to France as a child and trained as an engineer at ENSI Caen. After salaried work, he started a computer and data-acquisition company, then used its sale to build telecommunications ventures. Normandnet and Altitude Telecom established his reputation in business internet and wireless broadband, including early WiMax deployment.

Rivière sold Altitude Telecom in 2010 but retained the family holding and redirected it toward fibre infrastructure, enterprise connectivity and property. Altitude Infra grew through public-network contracts and acquisitions, while his daughter Dorothée Lebarbier progressively assumed leadership and later became group chief executive. The reorganized group continued to operate fibre infrastructure and enterprise-connectivity subsidiaries alongside its property interests.

Altitude Infra grew through public-network contracts and acquisitions, while his daughter Dorothée Lebarbier progressively assumed leadership and later became group chief executive. The reorganized group continued to operate fibre infrastructure and enterprise-connectivity subsidiaries alongside its property interests.
